c74object.name: evi.clipper~
c74object.digest: Antialiased clipping algorithms for your audio
c74object.description:
evi.clipper~ is a 'max define' for the evi_clipper.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.clipper~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
A collection of four antialiased clipping algorithms: hard clip, soft clip, diode clip, asymmetric clip. Hard and soft are better antialiased and can take higher input gain before aliasing than the diode and asymmetric clippers. To be used whenever clamping of audio is required, evi.clipper~ should do a good job of protecting your precious audio.

inlet.digest: Inlet #1: Audio In that must be treated nicely

outlet.digest: Outlet #1: Anti Aliased Clipped Audio Out

attribute.name: clip
attribute.description: Select the clipping function used. 0=hard (default), 1=soft, 2=diode, 3=asymmetric. 'Hard' is the equivalent of [clip~ -1. 1], 'soft' is the equivalent of [tanh~], 'diode' is a static model of a 12AX7, 'aymmetric' is a static version of Laurent de Soras' 'Gloubi Boulga'.

attribute.name: oversampling
attribute.description: Regardless of this setting, hard and soft clippers are 2nd order antiderivatives and thus already have excellent behaviour with @oversampling=0. Oversampling=1 is 2x oversampling, oversampling=2 is 4x oversampling.

c74object.discussion: This object is for all those MSP users who use [clip~ -1. 1.] or [tanh~] at the end of their audio chains. You should avoid doing this - it can destroy your audio and alias like hell. Use evi.clipper~ instead. It can anti-alias very large gain inputs whilst retaining the clipping functionality you seek.
